title: FactorIA factoria.json
description: Project file at the root of every FactorIA game. Unknown keys are kept but ignored by the engine.

name.description: Human-readable game name shown in window titles and stores.

id.description: Reverse-DNS identifier used for mobile bundles, e.g. "com.example.spacedodge".

engine.description: Engine version the game was made with, e.g. "0.1".

mainScene.description: Project-relative path of the scene loaded at startup, e.g. "scenes/main.scene.json".

display.description: Window and design-resolution settings. The game always renders at the design resolution.

scaleMode.description: How the design resolution maps to the window: fit (keep aspect, letterbox), stretch (fill the window, distort), expand (keep aspect, grow the visible area on the long axis), pixel-perfect (integer scaling, letterbox). Default "fit". The loader also accepts any capitalisation and "pixelPerfect".

vsync.description: Synchronize presentation with the display refresh.

pixelArt.description: Use nearest-neighbour filtering when scaling the final image.

actions.description: Named input actions. Each maps to a list of bindings: key names ("Space", "A", "Left"), "MouseLeft"/"MouseRight"/"MouseMiddle", "Touch", gamepad buttons ("GamepadA", "GamepadStart", "GamepadDpadLeft"...) and gamepad half axes ("GamepadLeftStickLeft", "GamepadRightStickUp", "GamepadRightTrigger"...). Gamepad bindings match any connected pad.

deadzone.description: Gamepad deadzone for sticks (radial) and triggers (default 0.2): pushes below it count as 0 and the rest is rescaled to 0..1. Raise it for worn sticks that drift, lower it for precise ones.

icon.description: Game icon: the project-relative path of a square PNG or JPG image, e.g. "assets/icon.png" (forward slashes, inside the project folder). 1024x1024 recommended; it should be at least 512x512 (smaller or non-square images give a warning, a non-square one is centered on a transparent square). Every export generates what its platform needs from this one image: the .icns of a macOS app, the exe icon on Windows, the launcher icons of Android, the App Store icon of iOS, the PNG of a Linux build. Each platform can use another image through export.<platform>.icon. No icon at all means the platform's default icon plus a warning on export. On Windows and Linux the same image is also the icon of the game window at run time. Edited by the editor's Platform settings window.

plugins.description: Native plugins of the game: libraries in C, C++ or any language with a C ABI that add commands and script functions (plugins.<name>.<function>(...)) through fa_plugin.h, e.g. store and platform SDKs. Each key is a plugin name (lower-case letters, digits and underscores; its commands are <name>.<verb>). `factoria run`, the editor and tests load the build for this computer from the plugin's folder; `factoria export` copies or links the build for the target platform into the game. `factoria validate` checks that every build exists. Created with project.new_plugin. See docs/EXTENDING.md, "Native plugins".

path.description: The plugin's folder: project-relative, absolute, or with ${VARIABLE} parts replaced by environment variables, so that a private SDK can live outside the game's repository ("${STEAMWORKS_PLUGIN}"). It holds one build per platform: windows/<name>.dll, macos/lib<name>.dylib, linux/lib<name>.so (each next to the libraries it needs), android/ (a Gradle library module with build.gradle, or .aar files) and ios/iphoneos/lib<name>.a plus ios/iphonesimulator/lib<name>.a.

platforms.description: The platforms the plugin is built for (default: the game's `platforms`, or all five). On other platforms the game runs without it and plugins.<name> is undefined.

platform.description: Store and platform services of the game: achievements, stats, leaderboards, cloud saves and in-app purchases behind one scripting API (`platform` from "factoria", docs/PLATFORM.md). This section declares what the game has, so that ids are checked before a request leaves the game and each store gets its own id for the same entry ("ids"). Every key is optional. Which store answers is chosen by the native plugins the game declares ("plugins") and by "backend"; development runs, tests and the MCP server use a deterministic fake store. `factoria validate` reports every problem with how to fix it.

backend.description: Which native plugin provides the store backend: "auto" (the default: the only plugin that registers one), a plugin name ("steam"), or an object per platform ({"windows": "steam", "macos": "steam", "linux": "steam", "ios": "apple"}). Needed only when several plugins offer a backend. Without any, development runs use the fake backend and exported games get no platform services.

achievements.description: The achievements of the game: platform.achievements.unlock("<id>").

id.description: The id scripts use (platform.<service>.<function>("<id>")): 1-64 letters, digits, '_', '.' or '-', unique within its section.

description.description: What the player did to earn it.

hidden.description: Hidden until unlocked (the stores' secret achievements).

ids.description: The id each store uses for this entry, keyed by backend name: {"steam": "ACH_WIN_ONE_GAME", "apple": "com.studio.game.first_win"}. Without an entry for a backend, the id is used as it is.

stats.description: Numbers the store keeps for the player: platform.stats.get("<id>"), set, add.

id.description: The id scripts use (platform.<service>.<function>("<id>")): 1-64 letters, digits, '_', '.' or '-', unique within its section.

ids.description: The id each store uses for this entry, keyed by backend name: {"steam": "ACH_WIN_ONE_GAME", "apple": "com.studio.game.first_win"}. Without an entry for a backend, the id is used as it is.

id.description: The id scripts use (platform.<service>.<function>("<id>")): 1-64 letters, digits, '_', '.' or '-', unique within its section.

order.description: "descending": a higher score is better (points); "ascending": a lower one is (times).

ids.description: The id each store uses for this entry, keyed by backend name: {"steam": "ACH_WIN_ONE_GAME", "apple": "com.studio.game.first_win"}. Without an entry for a backend, the id is used as it is.

id.description: The id scripts use (platform.<service>.<function>("<id>")): 1-64 letters, digits, '_', '.' or '-', unique within its section.

type.description: "consumable" can be bought again (gems), "nonConsumable" once (remove ads), "subscription" renews.

title.description: The product's name. Real stores show their own; the fake backend uses this.

description.description: What it gives. Real stores show their own; the fake backend uses this.

price.description: The price the fake backend shows (real stores give their own).

currency.description: The currency of `price` for the fake backend.

ids.description: The id each store uses for this entry, keyed by backend name: {"steam": "ACH_WIN_ONE_GAME", "apple": "com.studio.game.first_win"}. Without an entry for a backend, the id is used as it is.

export.description: Per-platform export settings, committed with the game. Every field is optional and defaults are applied; a field equal to its default is best left out. Unknown keys inside a platform object only give a warning (with a "did you mean"). Edited by the editor's Platform settings window; machine-specific settings (Android SDK and JDK folders, keystore passwords) are never stored here but in ~/.factoria/export.json. See docs/EXPORTING.md, "Platform settings".

scriptBytecode.description: Release builds of the desktop platforms (factoria export --release for windows, macos, linux): compile the scripts (.js) to QuickJS bytecode inside the game pack instead of shipping their source. Default true. The compiled scripts only run on the FactorIA version that wrote them (a game that meets another version says so and asks for a new export), keep their file names and line numbers in error messages, and leave out the source text. false ships the scripts as plain source in the pack. A script with a syntax error is shipped as source with a warning. Without --release, and on Android and iOS, the setting changes nothing. See docs/EXPORTING.md, "Release build".

icon.description: Icon of the Windows export, replacing the project's top-level "icon" there. Same rules as the top-level "icon". Empty or absent = use the project's "icon".

macos.description: macOS export settings (factoria export --platform macos): fields of the app's Info.plist.

icon.description: Icon of the macOS export, replacing the project's top-level "icon" there. Same rules as the top-level "icon". Empty or absent = use the project's "icon".

category.description: Mac App Store category of the app (LSApplicationCategoryType in Info.plist), e.g. "public.app-category.games" (the default), "public.app-category.action-games", "public.app-category.puzzle-games", "public.app-category.role-playing-games".

minimumSystemVersion.description: Oldest macOS the app runs on (LSMinimumSystemVersion in Info.plist), as "major.minor". Default "11.0", which is also the lowest value: FactorIA's macOS player needs macOS 11 or newer.

copyright.description: Copyright notice shown in the app's About information (NSHumanReadableCopyright in Info.plist), e.g. "Copyright 2026 My Studio". Default: none.

icon.description: Icon of the Linux export, replacing the project's top-level "icon" there. Same rules as the top-level "icon". Empty or absent = use the project's "icon".

categories.description: Menu categories of the game's .desktop file (the Categories= line; FactorIA joins the entries with ';'). Default ["Game"].

icon.description: Icon of the Android export, replacing the project's top-level "icon" there. Same rules as the top-level "icon". Empty or absent = use the project's "icon". The launcher icons are generated from it, unless adaptiveIcon says otherwise.

format.description: What the Android export produces: "apk" (default; runs the Gradle build and copies <game>.apk next to the project; debug builds are <game>-debug.apk), "aab" (an Android App Bundle for Google Play) or "gradle" (only the Gradle project, to open in Android Studio).

adaptiveIcon.description: Layers of the Android adaptive icon (Android 8+). Absent = the game icon scaled into the safe zone over a white background.

foreground.description: Project-relative path of the foreground layer: a square PNG of the whole 108dp layer (432x432 recommended) in which only the inner 66dp circle is guaranteed to stay visible, with a transparent background. Default: the game icon scaled into that safe zone (66/108 of the layer).

background.description: Background of the adaptive icon: a colour written "#RRGGBB" (default "#FFFFFF"), or the project-relative path of a square image (432x432 recommended) that fills the whole layer.

monochrome.description: Optional project-relative path of a square single-colour PNG with transparency (432x432 recommended) that Android 13+ tints for themed icons. Default: none, so the icon is not themed.

versionCode.description: Android versionCode: a whole number that must grow with every upload to Google Play. Default: derived from "version" (1.2.3 -> 10203; each part is capped at 99).

minSdk.description: Lowest Android API level the app installs on. Default 26 (Android 8.0), which is also the lowest value; it must not exceed targetSdk.

targetSdk.description: Android API level the app is built and tested against (also the compileSdk). Default 36; Google Play requires a recent one for new apps and updates. Must be at least minSdk.

permissions.description: Extra <uses-permission> entries of the manifest, for permissions the game's scripts or features need (the engine itself needs none). Default: none.

signing.description: Release signing of the Android export. The keystore PASSWORDS never go in the project: they come from the FACTORIA_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD and FACTORIA_ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD environment variables, or from the machine settings file ~/.factoria/export.json. Release builds without a keystore are signed with the debug key and warn.

keystore.description: Path of the keystore file (.keystore or .jks): project-relative, or absolute (keystores are better kept outside the repository). Create one with the editor's "Create keystore..." button or the JDK's keytool.

alias.description: Alias of the signing key inside the keystore (the -alias given to keytool), e.g. "upload".

icon.description: Icon of the iOS export, replacing the project's top-level "icon" there. Same rules as the top-level "icon". Empty or absent = use the project's "icon". The App Store icon is the icon composed over iconBackground.

iconBackground.description: Colour "#RRGGBB" the icon is composed over: the App Store rejects icons with transparency, so any transparent pixels of the icon take this colour. Default "#FFFFFF".

teamId.description: Apple developer Team ID (10 capital letters and digits, shown at developer.apple.com/account under Membership details), used to sign device builds. Default: the FA_IOS_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM environment variable of build_ios.sh, which takes precedence when set.

buildNumber.description: Build number of the app (CFBundleVersion): up to three whole numbers separated by dots, e.g. "42" or "1.2.3"; it must grow with every App Store upload of the same version. Default: the project's "version".

feedbackFile.description: Project-relative path of the engine feedback log (default ENGINE_FEEDBACK.json).
